strings.name: Valentino Rossi
strings.summary: Valentino Rossi won nine Grand Prix motorcycle world championships, seven in the premier class. His career crossed the two-stroke 500cc and four-stroke MotoGP eras, while his VR46 network developed young riders. After leaving MotoGP in 2021 he turned to GT cars. In 2026, following two World Endurance Championship seasons, he returned to WRT’s full GT World Challenge Europe programme.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Multiple motorcycle world titles, longevity and rider development broadened the sport’s influence.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Nine world championships
strings.highlights.h1.text: Titles in 125cc in 1997, 250cc in 1999 and seven premier-class seasons established sustained success across categories.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Influenced by his racing father, competed in karting and minimoto before progressing through Italian competition to Grands Prix.
strings.highlights.h2.title: The VR46 development network
strings.highlights.h2.text: Youth training, a training base and racing teams support young Italian riders and extend his influence beyond personal results.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Return to European GT focus
strings.timeline.t1.text: Raced WRT’s BMW M4 GT3 in the European Sprint and Endurance Cups after competing in WEC in 2024–25.
strings.timeline.t2.title: A new GT racing phase
strings.timeline.t2.text: Began a full GT season, continuing competition on four wheels and subsequently becoming a BMW works driver.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Final MotoGP race
strings.timeline.t3.text: Completed his last MotoGP event in Valencia, ending his premier-class motorcycle racing career.
strings.timeline.t4.title: VR46 Academy
strings.timeline.t4.text: Established the rider academy to develop younger competitors through structured training and racing support.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Ninth world title
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won another MotoGP championship with Yamaha, his ninth Grand Prix world title overall.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Championship on switching to Yamaha
strings.timeline.t6.text: Left Honda for Yamaha and won the MotoGP title in his first season, retaining it the following year.
strings.timeline.t7.title: 500cc world champion
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won the final 500cc championship with Honda, becoming a premier-class champion.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Grand Prix beginnings
strings.timeline.t8.text: Entered the 125cc world championship, winning that title the next year and the 250cc championship in 1999.
